title: Westbrook City Council — Special Meeting

fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. Summarization necessarily condenses and selects; for complete context, nuance, and anything not covered here, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: President Jennifer Munro, Vice President Michael Shaughnessy, Brian McCambridge, Victor Chau, Anna Turcotte, Amy Faulkingham, Gary Rairdon. Mayor David Morse also attended.

blocks.x: Mayor's Message: Staff Transitions
Finance Department, Assistant City Administrator & Staff Recognitions
Discussion Summary

Finance Department: Finance Director Tressina Germani departed after nearly 14 years with the City. Deputy Finance Director Laura King was appointed Interim Finance Director. She has been with the City since 2023 and was previously a Portland Water District financial analyst for seven years.

The Tax Collector position is also vacant, and state statute places that obligation on the Finance Director (see Order 2026-28). To bridge the gap, the City added two vendors to its approved vendor list (Order 2026-30). They are the Maine Municipal Association (part-time consulting support, $150/hour) and Robert Half Recruiters & Employment Agency (temporary front-line staffing, ~$35/hour).
Assistant City Administrator: Jennie Franceschi was promoted to Assistant City Administrator. She has been Director of Planning & Code Enforcement since 2016.
She was also the Maine Association of Planners' 2025 Planner of the Year. She will continue part-time as Planning Director until a replacement is hired. Full transition is expected around May 1.
City Clerk recognition: Ellis Ledoux received the Certified Clerk of Maine designation from the Maine Town and City Clerks Association after a three-year certification process.
In memoriam: the Mayor noted the recent death of longtime community volunteer Judith Reedman. She served on numerous city boards and with Rotary.
Key Decisions
Informational — no vote taken.
Action Items
None.
Public Comment (First)
Non-Municipal Comment & a New Business's Parking Inquiry
Discussion Summary

A resident urged support for a letter-writing campaign. It asks Pope Leo XIV to convene world religious leaders about the Iran conflict. This is not a Westbrook municipal matter, and it drew no Council response or action.
Hayley Bankis is facilities manager for the Center for Autism and Related Disorders. It is a pediatric therapy provider new to Westbrook, at 39 Mechanic St., Suite 300.

Bankis asked about the process for requesting 15-minute parking in front of the building. The parking would safely accommodate children with disabilities who cannot safely walk from the current lot. City Administrator Holmes directed her to email the City Clerk's office to coordinate with the relevant departments.
Key Decisions
Informational — no vote taken.
Action Items
None.
Orders of the Day — Second & Final Reading
Orders 2026-25, -26, -27 — School Bond/Capital-Fund Reallocations & Radio Equipment (Consent)
Discussion Summary
All were first read (the first of two required votes) at the Mar. 2, 2026 meeting. They cover:
Reallocating up to $365,000 in unspent Spring 2025 bond proceeds (money the City borrowed) to Canal/Congin School projects.
Reallocating $385,000 in unused Westbrook High School capital funds to security-system and window/door projects.
$678,746.01 for Phase 3 public safety radio equipment.
See that meeting's summary for full detail. Moved together; no discussion.
Key Decisions
Passed together by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
New Business — Liquor License
Bombay Bistro (3 Vallee Square)
Public hearing held.
Discussion Summary
It is owned by Blessing Hospitality LLC in partnership with Antonio, Nobel Rugo, and Peter Mutima, and managed by James Bowser.

Councilor Rairdon flagged a discrepancy between the ownership percentages on the state application and on the supplemental ownership form. For example, one partner was listed at 35% on one form and 33% on the other.

Antonio explained the differences reflect recent equity changes as new investor-partners joined after the initial application was filed. The Clerk's office agreed to confirm the correct figures with the State before the license takes effect.
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Brian McCambridge.
Action Items
None.
Orders of the Day — One Reading Required
Order 2026-28 — Confirming Laura King as Tax Collector
Found on page 57 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Releases former Tax Collector Dena Lebeda from liability for uncollected tax years April 2020 through April 2025. It recommits those balances to Interim Finance Director/Tax Collector Laura King by warrant (the formal order to collect them). Councilor Rairdon noted the difficulty of a new finance director absorbing tax-collector duties without a deputy in place. He expressed hope the department returns to full staffing soon.
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Michael Shaughnessy, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-29 — Amending Order 2026-10 — Additional HVAC Expenditure
Found on page 69 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Confirms an additional $1,913.37 emergency expenditure to ABM Mechanical, Inc. for heating, ventilation and air conditioning repairs at the Public Services Facility. This came after a leak was discovered in a section of radiant heating during the boiler replacement work (outside the original project scope).
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Amy Faulkingham, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-30 — Amending the Annual Vendor List
Found on page 72 of the packet.
Discussion Summary
Adds Robert Half Recruiters & Employment Agency and the Maine Municipal Association as approved vendors to keep Finance Department staffing steady (see Mayor's Message above).

Councilor Chau asked whether spending over $10,000 needed a Council vote and why no cost figures were provided. The administration said spending was nearing the $5,000 limit requiring Council approval unless a vendor is on the annual list.
Interim Finance Director Laura King and City Administrator Holmes confirmed this is a temporary bridge, not a long-term arrangement. They agreed to keep the Council updated on costs.
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Brian McCambridge.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-31 — Amending Order 2025-135 — City Hall Renovation
Found on page 76 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Authorizes an additional $3,100 to Harnois Painting Company for painting work. The work is in the City Administrator, Assistant City Administrator, City Clerk, and Deputy City Clerk offices. It extends an earlier $8,000 authorization for common-area appearance improvements.
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Amy Faulkingham, seconded by Michael Shaughnessy.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-32 — Food Security Grant Program Ordinance (As Amended)
Found on page 80 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Amends the City's Code of Ordinances (its local laws), Chapter 33 (Finances). It adds a formal, more equitable and transparent Food Security Grant Program for allocating funds to social-service agencies. This replaces the City's prior ad hoc (case-by-case) approach. It was adopted as amended by the Finance Committee earlier the same evening.
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-33 — Uncollectible Ambulance Debt Write-Off Policy
Found on page 90 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Allows the Finance Department to write off, on an annual basis, ambulance-billing receivables (money owed to the City) more than seven years old. That is the point at which debt-collection industry standards consider medical debt no longer reasonably collectible. The City currently carries more than $1.4 million in unpaid ambulance billing debt dating from 2003 to the present.

Under the policy, a write-off removes accounts from active receivables but does not forgive the debt. An initial “true-up” will address the existing backlog, with one additional year written off annually going forward.
Councilor Rairdon asked for an annual report of the amount written off. The administration agreed to provide it.
Key Decisions
Approved by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Brian McCambridge, seconded by Amy Faulkingham.
Action Items
None.
Orders of the Day — Two Readings Required
Order 2026-34 — Community Center Gym Floor Refurbishment
Found on page 96 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Accepts a $43,469 donation from the Cornelia Warren Community Association and a $14,000 donation from Paper City Hoops. It authorizes a $57,469 expenditure to New England Sports Floors (Lowell, MA) for the refurbishment. Several councilors thanked both donor organizations.
Key Decisions
Passed first reading by show of hands, none opposed. Moved by Michael Shaughnessy, seconded by Amy Faulkingham.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-35 — Credere Associates Task Order No. 8 — Riverwalk North
Found on page 100 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Authorizes up to $211,500 to Credere Associates for permitting assistance and design services on the Riverwalk North Brownfields cleanup project. The cost is reimbursable through the City's FY2024 $4 million U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Brownfields Cleanup Grant. This is the next phase of the project previewed in the Feb. 23 Annual Project Updates presentation.
Key Decisions
Passed first reading by show of hands, none opposed. Moved by Amy Faulkingham, seconded by Gary Rairdon.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-36 — Brown Street Culvert Engineering Design
Found on page 105 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Authorizes $21,500 to Sebago Technics to update a 2015 culvert-reconstruction design to current stream-crossing standards. The project is near the Cottage Place Pump Station end of Brown Street. An earlier state grant-funding bid for the project was unsuccessful. The updated design is intended to support a future funding application.
Key Decisions
Passed first reading by show of hands, none opposed. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
Closing
Public Comment (Second) & Adjournment
Discussion Summary
No further public comment. No referrals, no committee reports, no executive session (a closed, private session).
Key Decisions
Motion to adjourn approved by show of hands, none opposed. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
